chunks_canon.text: This method sets out how the price of a parcel is determined from its size, its weight and its destination zone.
It applies to every parcel handed in at a counter. Pallets and letters are outside its scope.
The method is reviewed once a year by the pricing committee.
Actual weight (AW) is the weight of the parcel in kilograms as shown by the scale.
Dimensional weight (DW) is a weight derived from the volume of the parcel.
Chargeable weight (CW) is the weight on which the price is based.
The zone is the destination area of the parcel: Local, National or Abroad.
The dimensional weight is obtained from the length L, the width W and the height H of the parcel, measured in centimetres.
The divisor of 5000 is fixed and is not varied by zone.
The chargeable weight is the larger of the actual weight and the dimensional weight: CW = max(AW, DW).
The chargeable weight is never taken below 0.5 kilograms.
Weights are not rounded before the price is calculated.
Each zone has a base rate and a rate per kilogram, as set out in Table 1.

chunks_canon.caption: Table 1. Rates by zone
chunks_canon.text:
Zone; Base rate; Rate per kg
Local; 3.20; 0.85
National; 4.90; 1.10
Abroad; 9.50; 2.75
Rates are stated in the currency of the counter and exclude tax.
The price before surcharge is the base rate plus the rate per kilogram times the chargeable weight: P = B + R * CW.
B and R are taken from Table 1 for the zone of the parcel.
A fuel surcharge of 12.5% is added to the price before surcharge: S = P * (1 + 0.125).
The surcharge rate is set by the pricing committee and is the same for all zones.
A customer who hands in n parcels at once receives a discount rate of 1% per parcel, capped at 20%: D = min(0.2, 0.01 * n).
The discount is applied to the price after surcharge.

chunks_canon.caption: Figure 1. Discount rate by number of parcels
chunks_canon.text: Discount rate against number of parcels
The final price is never below 4.50, whatever the zone and the discount.
Final prices are rounded to 2 decimals.
Changes to Table 1 are approved by the pricing committee and recorded in the change log.
Questions about this method are answered by the pricing office.

chunks_doc.text: This document describes how the parcelcost package implements the parcel pricing method.
The package is maintained by the pricing office and released once a year.
The function dim_weight derives the dimensional weight from length, width and height with the fixed divisor of 5000.
The function chargeable_weight returns the larger of actual weight and dimensional weight and never returns less than 0.5 kilograms.
The function parcel_price looks up the base rate and the rate per kilogram of the zone in the table zone_rates.

chunks_doc.caption: Table A. Rates held in the package
chunks_doc.text:
Zone; Base rate; Rate per kg
Local; 3.20; 0.85
National; 4.90; 1.10
Abroad; 9.50; 2.75
The price before surcharge equals the base rate plus the rate per kilogram times the chargeable weight.
A fuel surcharge of 12.5% is added to the price before surcharge.
The volume discount is 1% per parcel and is capped at 20%.
The final price is never below 4.50 and is rounded to 2 decimals.
Unit tests cover the dimensional weight and the minimum price.
The tests are run before every release.
Questions are answered by the pricing office.

#' @export

#' Dimensional weight
#'
#' Weight derived from the volume of a parcel: \deqn{DW = \frac{L \cdot W \cdot H}{5000}}
#' @param l length in centimetres
#' @param w width in centimetres
#' @param h height in centimetres
#' @param divisor the fixed divisor, 5000
#' @export

model_units.name: dim_weight
dim_weight
model_units.text: l * w * h / divisor
